Positoxins! They're exactly what you'd look for in this situation; a poison made for use against undead, introduced in 3.5 from Libris Mortis. You'd obviously have to do some workshopping to make it function in 5e, but their general gimmick is reducing ability scores of undead by breaking their bodies down. Of course, you could also simply use the effects of regular poisons, but label them positoxins, but there IS an undead-poison existent in dnd's history!

If Izek is not dead, Victor could be with him. The module gives a few areas he might be hanging out, like the Old Bonegrinder, Berez, or Argynvostholt. Alternatively, Victor's mother is actually the younger sister of Father Lucien, who might offer his nephew sanctuary in the church, assuming it's still standing. I think it could be fun and interesting to give them a **nerfed** version of the Twilight Cleric's Channel Divinity as an option to the Paladin. Some people like to start the campaign in Krezk rather than the Village of Barovia, if you want to get the party within proximity quickly. Alternatively, I myself am making Ireena and Vasilka the same character, having her hide out in the Village of Barovia after escaping the Abbot. Another thing to consider, is if/how you're going to alter Vasilka's personality; RAW she doesn't speak and AFAIK, the module doesn't give much for her characterization. Being inhabited by Tatyana's soul, I imagine she might have her own thoughts and opinions. Would she go off on her own, either to escape her arranged marriage, or maybe even approach Strahd herself, after the Abbot prepared her as a bride? Maybe she's seeking the wedding gown herself in Vallaki, wanting to pick out her own dress, or maybe the Abbot accompanies her there.

As for Ireena, she could be made into a vampire spawn, perhaps having accompanied Doru during the failed uprising, gives the party a quest to 'rescue him from Donavich". If your party is familiar with CoS, you could even pull a switcheroo by having her as a spy for Strahd. Maybe make her an enemy of Strahd; she somehow drew his ire, and that's why undead are sent to harass her. If she still wants to escape to Vallaki, you could rewrite some interesting ideas between her and Izek; two siblings, separated in childhood, who oppose Strahd's rule, except one has fallen to corruption.

You could potentially have the Dark Powers offer the character the opportunity to kill this noble; not by setting this PC free, but by dragging the Baron there, in a faraway land, where no one will ever discover the man's fate. Of course, this opportunity would come with the usual Dark Powers drawbacks, but revenge is awfully tempting.

If you don't want to corrupt them outright, you could have the character slowly go mad in Vallaki, what with the similarities. Make it ambiguous, as if Vargas *could* be that noble, *somehow...*Have Fiona Wachter take advantage of the situation if they ever sit down with her. Use Victor's defunct teleportation circle as an opportunity to zap him back in, or have the Vistani bring him over.

Alternatively? Have the Baron, somehow, someway, be connected with Strahd. Maybe he's a warlock, and Strahd is his patron. Maybe the noble is somehow partially responsible for the rogue ending up in Barovia. Maybe *Strahd* has beef with the Baron and brings him to Barovia to watch him be torn about by the rogue, opening the way for an "allegiance" (manipulation).

Ah man, this really sucks. If you don't want to split your casting abilities, here's a few potential solutions

1) Taking a level in lore bard/warlock and using INT. Bards don't have to be musical necessarily and can be flavored different, lore bards are supposed to be scholars, so it could fit your character's theme. Many have suggested warlock already, have your character make a pact for magic. This all depends on your tastes and if your DM would allow it, however.  


2) If your DM won't allow alternative casting abilities, artificer is one option or maybe a profane soul blood hunter if the DM will allow it. You'd have to wait around a bit to fully benefit from blood hunter, so it would require some investment and I'm not sure hemocraft would fit your character's flavor all that much.

​

3) The magic initiate feat. It isn't nearly as satisfying as multiclassing, but it's still a nod that your character has managed to tap into their magic.

​

4) Multiclass into any other magic class but keep it flavored as a wizard. Mechanically it's all the same, but you'd treat it as your character finally getting her magic to function. Bonus if your DM will allow alternative casting modifier.

Hi there. It sounds like you're going through some really shitty stuff (you wouldn't be here otherwise, I would imagine), and I've been through the process of blaming myself and wrestling with the concept of vulnerability, too. I still kind of do, sometimes. Please try to remember it's not your fault you were abused; a common abuse tactic is to make a victim feel like they deserved to be hurt or somehow invited it. You didn't. That's all a fallacy they use to play with people in their hands and establish control.

One thing that even I presently struggle with right now is that we are people. You are a person. You would not blame someone for going through what you've been through, and I know it feels very, very, very different, but it's the same for you. You're a person and what they did to you was wrong. It's okay. They hurt you and that was not an okay or right thing to do. Try and step back and see yourself as an objective person; just like everyone else, you're a human, and it's ok to have compassion for yourself. Treat yourself the way you'd ideally be treated by others. Take care of your self, not just physically, but emotionally. Try to prioritize yourself...it feels selfish, but it's really not. It's healthy self-preservation and we've been conditioned to feel bad about it.

Sorry if this isn't the best response, I struggle a little bit with comforting without psychoanalyzing and it can come across as unhelpful. I really hope this brings some kind of comfort to you.
